texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Q: I’m working on our product management career ladder, and I’m looking for examples of how other companies do it.
texts.text: Q: I’m working on our product management career ladder, and I’m looking for examples of how other companies do it.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Career ladders (a.k.a. leveling frameworks, career tracks, competencies, etc.) have long been secretive and mysterious. I’m not totally sure why. I don’t see how sharing these publicly gives anyone a competitive advantage, and every new company ends up scratching their heads and coming up with something new. Why do we do this to ourselves? It’s especially painful for product management—a role that is already so inconsistently defined and evaluated.
texts.text: Career ladders (a.k.a. leveling frameworks, career tracks, competencies, etc.) have long been secretive and mysterious. I’m not totally sure why.
